clue.text: Sort of light stick used in a game played by RoSPA?

definitions.meaning: a small stick that strikes only on its own box, used to light a fire
a contest staged by Britain's accident-prevention society would be a match about staying safe

explanation.surface: A firelighting stick turns up in some contest played by a woman called Rosa.
explanation.walkthrough: RoSPA is the Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents, a British charity, so a match it played would be all about safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike-on-the-box lighting stick is the standard household type sold for safe use.

clue.text: Kept going without a pause

definitions.meaning: unbroken and continuous, as a long-held note

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a past tense for maintained and an adjective for continuous or unbroken.

clue.text: Being so mirthful, Eve's fit to bust

indicators.note: bust means break apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Eve is so merry she is fit to burst.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's here does give its S, since EVES plus FIT is the seven-letter pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive means jolly and celebratory, a synonym for merry.

clue.text: Out of debt, ready to get toy for a child

indicators.note: the letters come out of their order, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone freed from debt is ready to buy a child a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of debt' reads as solvency, but 'Out of' is the signal to rearrange DEBT and READY.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed bear is the classic cuddly plaything given to small children.

clue.text: Ape number 1000110001100

parts.note: the long figure splits into 1000, 1, 1000, 1, 100, each written as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An ape is identified by a long catalogue number.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals M is 1000, I is 1 and C is 100, so the string 1000-1-1000-1-100 spells out the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy them, which is exactly what an imitator does.

clue.text: Gifts of great value in ancient times

definitions.text: of great value in ancient times
definitions.meaning: large units of weight and money used in the ancient world, as in the biblical parable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means natural aptitudes and also the heavy silver or gold units of ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Swings on a door post

parts.note: read as the thing on which a door swings, fixed to its post, not a child swinging on one

explanation.definitionFit: A pivoting metal joint fixed to the frame is what lets a door turn open and shut.

clue.text: Strongpoints, as it were, controlled by elephants

definitions.text: Strongpoints, as it were, controlled by elephants

parts.words: Strongpoints, as it were, controlled by elephants
parts.note: strongpoints are fortified positions, but here they are literally strong pointed things wielded by elephants

explanation.definitionFit: Elephants' long ivory teeth are hard pointed weapons, punningly their strong points.

clue.text: Opens a tourist attraction in London

definitions.text: Opens a tourist attraction in London

parts.words: Opens a tourist attraction in London
parts.note: seems to describe a ribbon-cutting, but means a London sight that itself opens, raising its roadway for ships

explanation.definitionFit: The Thames bascule crossing by the Tower of London lifts its two halves to let tall ships pass.

clue.text: Tip fish&the last of the chips in the stew!

parts.note: to tip rubbish is to dump it
the ling is a long cod-like sea fish

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone throws fish and the leftover chips into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice, but it is a verb, to dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough balls cooked on top of a stew are what you find floating in it.

clue.text: Immediately after, the winner gets this award

definitions.text: Immediately after, the winner gets this award

parts.words: Immediately after, the winner gets this award
parts.note: read as the prize for whoever finishes immediately after the winner, in second place

explanation.definitionFit: Second place in an Olympic-style contest earns the runner-up's prize, below gold.

clue.text: You want vigour to do something in this fashion

definitions.text: You want vigour to do something in this fashion

parts.words: You want vigour to do something in this fashion
parts.note: want means lack, so this is how you do something when you lack energy

explanation.definitionFit: Doing a task tiredly, with no energy left, is doing it in a jaded, exhausted way.

clue.text: Get a solid lump out of the liquid!

definitions.text: Get a solid lump out of the liquid!

parts.words: Get a solid lump out of the liquid!
parts.note: sounds like fishing something out of a liquid, but means the liquid itself setting into a solid mass

explanation.definitionFit: To set or clot is for a liquid such as fat or blood to thicken into a solid.

clue.text: Use soap and water like this afterwards

definitions.text: Use soap and water like this afterwards

parts.words: Use soap and water like this afterwards
parts.note: the step that follows soaping: water alone washes the suds away

explanation.definitionFit: Washing off soap with clean water after scrubbing is the final step of washing.

clue.text: About sex&vice back in Kent — there's too much:

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation goes inside the jumbled letters
about means around or astir, so the letters are moved around
back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Kent is a county in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Sex and vice in Kent: a moralist complains there's far too much of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent, the county south-east of London, stands for SE; 'back' reverses it and 'in' sets it inside the letters 'About' produces, EXCSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess means beyond what is proper, so going over the limit is the sense.

clue.text: Scarf for a dummy!

definitions.meaning: a baby's rubber teat to suck, called a pacifier in America

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a warm woollen neckerchief and a baby's soother, besides one who consoles.

clue.text: Apart from other patients, you'll be alone in this hospital

definitions.text: Apart from other patients, you'll be alone in this hospital

parts.words: Apart from other patients, you'll be alone in this hospital
parts.note: describes a fever hospital where infectious patients are kept separate from everyone else

explanation.definitionFit: A fever hospital where contagious patients were kept apart was named for that separation.

clue.text: It holds the record for receiving wireless programmes, too

definitions.text: It holds the record for receiving wireless programmes, too

parts.words: It holds the record for receiving wireless programmes, too
parts.note: not a record-holder in sport but a cabinet holding a gramophone record as well as a wireless set

explanation.definitionFit: A mid-century cabinet combined a wireless receiver with a record player.

clue.text: Filthy and disgusting ex-pupil to act apart

parts.note: an ex-pupil is an old boy, abbreviated OB
read as 'act, a part': a part of an act of a play is a scene

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy behaves in a revolting way, standing aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act apart' must be split into 'act a part': a division of a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensively indecent or repugnant, so it fits filthy and disgusting.

clue.text: Attack leading to seizure, perhaps

parts.note: seems medical, a fit, but means a military assault meant to capture a stronghold

explanation.definitionFit: To take a fortress by force is to assault it, an attack that ends in capture.

clue.text: As it turned out, consumed -to make one replete!

indicators.note: turned out means rearranged, so the letters of the two words are mixed

parts.note: consumed means ate

explanation.surface: As it happened, someone ate enough to feel completely full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges AS IT to SATI.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate is to fill someone with food until they want no more.

clue.text: Low sort of bedstead, the top having been removed

indicators.note: sort of means a version of, so the letters are rearranged
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A low kind of bed frame has had its headboard taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: The top of 'the' is T: rearrange BEDSTEAD with that T removed. 'having been removed' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Debased means degraded or lowered in quality or character, so it means low.

clue.text: Not keen to be outspoken

definitions.meaning: keen means sharp, so not sharp

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both a dull edge and plain, frank speech.

clue.text: Pulls level with the other side, in the end

definitions.text: level with the other side, in the end
definitions.meaning: finishes matches all square with the opponents

explanation.definitionFit: The word means hauls along and also ends games tied with the opposition.

clue.text: Bound to follow boys on this adventure training

definitions.text: Bound to follow boys on this adventure training

parts.words: Bound to follow boys on this adventure training
parts.note: Bound is the word that comes next in the name of a famous outdoor training scheme for young people

explanation.walkthrough: Outward Bound is a British charity running outdoor adventure courses for young people.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheme's name is this word followed by Bound, a well-known adventure course.

clue.text: Natural feeling of obedient sailor on the order: "up spirits"?

definitions.text: Natural feeling of obedient sailor on the order: "up spirits"?

parts.words: Natural feeling of obedient sailor on the order: "up spirits"?
parts.note: Up Spirits was the navy's call for the daily rum ration, which would put any sailor in high spirits

explanation.walkthrough: Up Spirits was the Royal Navy call for the daily tot of rum, issued until 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: Being full of high spirits and lively joy is what the word means.

clue.text: Miscast Lear in one other play featuring him

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the rearranged name
a miscast actor is in the wrong part, so the letters of the name are wrongly placed

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A misjudged casting of King Lear puts one actor into a different Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miscast' rearranges LEAR to AREL; I goes 'in' it. The spirit Ariel appears in The Tempest, another Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero's airy spirit is the character found in The Tempest, a Shakespeare play other than King Lear.

clue.text: Sick wood cutter, presumably!

parts.note: a surgeon cuts, so one who operates on diseased timber is a cutter of sick wood

explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who cuts out diseased limbs is a doctor who operates on trees.
